jobs.title: Research Engineer / Research Scientist, Human Flourishing
jobs.description:
Post-training - San Francisco

**About the Team**

The Human Flourishing team’s mission is to ensure AI systems understand and advance human flourishing. As AI becomes more capable and plays a larger role in people’s lives, we want its human benefits to grow with its capabilities. The Human Flourishing team is part of the broader Personal AGI organization.

Our approach has two parts. Firstly, we measure and improve models’ understanding, capability, and propensity to act according to people’s values and to help them achieve their long-term goals. Secondly, we directly scale tangible impact for users in human domains like education and mental health, working across research, product, and partnerships to increase the benefits over a billion people experience weekly when they use ChatGPT.

Our recent work includes Beneficial RL, which investigates how training for beneficial behavior generalizes across settings, and MentalHealthBench, a benchmark developed with mental health experts to evaluate realistic conversations.

**About the Role**

We’re looking for an exceptional, hands-on researcher to turn difficult-to-define signals of long-term flourishing into measurable improvements in model behavior. You’ll help set research direction, build what is needed to test your ideas, and drive successful work into the models and products we ship.

We’re especially interested in researchers with deep experience improving frontier models through pretraining or reinforcement learning (RL) / post-training, especially on less verifiable problems, or researchers who combine strong LLM skills with deep expertise in domains like education or mental health. Prior experience in these domains is not required.

**In this role, you will**

* Develop scalable training methods across the training stack that improve how models understand people’s values, support their agency, and help them achieve long-term goals.
* Lead high-leverage research from an open question to a shipped improvement: choose a hard-to-define problem, iteratively define success, run experiments, and integrate into frontier models.
* Build RL environments for difficult-to-verify outcomes, and study whether beneficial behavior generalizes across settings.
* Create evaluations grounded in human expertise and feedback that reveal capability gaps, unintended incentives in RL, and failures that aggregate scores can miss.
* Test whether measures of model behavior predict better learning, wellbeing, and other long-term outcomes, and use those findings to guide training.
* Build new 0 1 capabilities in human domains that may have an increasing impact with upcoming increases in model intelligence and test-time compute.
* Partner with product teams, engineers, partnerships teams, and domain experts to deploy promising methods, measure their effects in real use, and turn what you learn into further improvements.
* Assess AI’s impacts on human flourishing at the scale of over a billion users.

**You might thrive in this role if you**

* Care deeply about helping AI improve people’s lives, and feel this is a responsibility that comes with increasingly capable models.
* Have an unusually strong research record in pretraining or RL / post-training research, especially in a hard-to-verify area; or combine strong LLM research skills with deep expertise in education, mental health, or a related field of human benefit.
* Are a hands-on builder who can turn ideas into rigorous experiments, write and debug code, and work directly with data and training infrastructure.
* Have the taste to choose consequential problems and actionable steps on the path to solving those problems.
* Take ownership of ambiguous problems and choose methods based on the impact they can deliver, including when the most useful work is unglamorous.
* Care about whether a capability will scale, generalize, and make it into the real world—not just whether it can be shown in a paper or prototype.
* Work well across disciplines and can grok the most important bottlenecks to scaling our impact in a multidisciplinary problem.

If you’re excited about ensuring AI systems advance human flourishing, we’d love to hear from you.

**About OpenAI**

OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core the full spectrum of humanity.

jobs.title: Principal Applied Scientist, Real-Time Conversational AI , AGI
jobs.description:
**DESCRIPTION**
---------------

We are looking for a Principal Applied Scientist to drive the research and development of real-time multimodal conversational AI. You will operate across two focus areas: advancing foundation models for speech and audio, and building the post-training systems (reward modeling, reinforcement learning) that shape natural, human-like conversational behavior.
  
  
You will be the expert in your area while contributing across the full model lifecycle — from pre-training and architecture design through post-training alignment and real-time deployment. You will work at the frontier of what's possible in conversational AI, with the compute, data, and runway to pursue problems that few teams in the world have the resources to tackle.
  
  
As a Principal Scientist, you will set the technical direction for your research area, influence the broader roadmap, and work closely with inference engineers to ensure your models are designed for real-time production deployment from inception.  
  
Key job responsibilities  
Foundation Model Scaling
  
  

* Build and train large-scale multimodal foundation models for real-time speech and audio generation, from architecture design through production-scale training

  

* Advance the scaling and efficiency of conversational modes, including the relationship between data, model size, and real time performance.

  

* Design model architectures informed by hardware constraints and inference requirements, working with inference engineers to ensure models are servable from inception

  

* Develop training methodologies for multimodal models that jointly process and generate speech, language, and audio in real-time streaming contexts

  
Post-Training & Reinforcement Learning
  
  

* Design and build reward models and reward functions for speech systems — capturing naturalness, fluency, conversational quality, and real-time responsiveness

  

* Develop and apply reinforcement learning methods to shape conversational behavior — teaching models natural timing, responsiveness, and fluid interaction

  

* Build the post-training pipeline from SFT through RL alignment, optimized for real-time multimodal outputs rather than text-only generation

  

* Design evaluation frameworks that capture the quality dimensions unique to real-time conversation

  
Real-Time Perception & Generation
  
  

* Advance the team's capabilities in real-time perception

  
  

* Work at the intersection of model architecture and production constraints to ensure multimodal capabilities function within hard real-time latency budgets

  
About the team  
We are a small, focused group of scientists and engineers building the next generation of real-time conversational AI at Amazon — models that interact naturally across speech and audio. We operate with the autonomy and pace of a research lab, backed by frontier-scale compute and a multi-year investment horizon.

**BASIC QUALIFICATIONS**
------------------------

* Experience distilling informal customer requirements into problem definitions, dealing with ambiguity and competing objectives
* PhD in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Electrical Engineering, Speech/Audio Processing, or equivalent quantitative field
* 10+ years of applied research experience (industry or combined academic + industry)
* Demonstrated experience training large-scale foundation models — hands-on involvement in scaling exercises, not just using pre-trained models
* Experience with multimodal model architectures that jointly process or generate across speech, text, and audio modalities
* Strong understanding of transformer architectures and their application to speech/audio domains
* Publication record at top-tier venues (NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, Interspeech, ICASSP, ACL, or equivalent)
* Demonstrated Principal/Staff+ scientific leadership — setting research direction, mentoring researchers, influencing multi-team decisions

**PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS**
----------------------------

* 10+ years of relevant work in industry or academia experience
* Hands-on experience building real-time AI systems — speech, audio, or video
* Track record with post-training methods: reinforcement learning, reward modeling, RLHF/RLAIF, or alignment techniques applied to generative models
* Experience with real-time interactive systems — models that handle concurrent input and output
* Experience building speech-to-speech or audio-to-audio generative models (codec models, autoregressive audio generation)
* Hands-on design of reward models or reward functions specifically for speech/audio quality, naturalness, or conversational behavior
* Experience with distributed training at scale — including parallelism strategies, training stability, and curriculum design
* Familiarity with hardware-informed model design — understanding how architecture choices affect inference latency, memory, and cost
* Background in speech recognition, speech synthesis (TTS), or speech enhancement
* Experience shipping research to production at scale — models serving real users, not just benchmark results
* Contributions to open-source speech/audio ML systems or widely used research codebases
* History of mentoring and growing research teams from individual contributors to technical leaders

Meta is seeking a Research Scientist to advance computer vision and AI research in support of Meta's broader mission to build the next generation of intelligent systems. In this role, you will conduct original research in areas such as visual perception, 3D scene understanding, image and video recognition, and fast models that operate on real-time video. You will collaborate with a multidisciplinary team of researchers and engineers to translate research insights into scalable AI capabilities that power Meta's products and platforms, from augmented and virtual reality experiences to large-scale content understanding systems.  
  
  

### **Research Scientist, Computer Vision (PhD) Responsibilities:**

* Design and conduct original research in computer vision, including 3D reconstruction, scene understanding, and generative image or video modeling
* Develop and train deep learning models using large-scale image and video datasets, iterating on architectures to improve accuracy, efficiency, and generalization
* Implement and evaluate novel computer vision algorithms, benchmarking against state-of-the-art methods on standard and internally curated datasets
* Contribute to the design and curation of training datasets and annotation pipelines for vision tasks
* Translate research findings into production-ready prototypes in collaboration with engineering teams
* Write and publish research results at leading computer vision and machine learning venues
* Participate in code reviews and contribute to shared research codebases, maintaining code quality and reproducibility
* Collaborate with cross-functional partners in product, engineering, and data science to align research directions with applied goals
* Instrument experiments with appropriate logging and evaluation metrics to support data-driven decision making
* Identify opportunities to improve existing vision systems and propose incremental or novel research directions to the team

  
  
  

### **Minimum Qualifications:**

* Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, relevant technical field, or equivalent practical experience
* Currently has, or is in the process of obtaining a Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, relevant technical field, or equivalent practical experience. Degree must be completed prior to joining Meta
* Currently has, or is in the process of obtaining, a PhD in computer vision, machine learning, computer science, or a related field
* 2+ years of research experience in computer vision, including work on 3D reconstruction, SLAM, or related areas
* Experience in developing and training deep learning models using frameworks such as PyTorch
* Experience implementing and evaluating computer vision algorithms and conducting rigorous experimental comparisons
* Experience communicating research findings through publications, technical reports, or presentations to peers
* Must obtain work authorization in the country of employment at the time of hire, and maintain ongoing work authorization during employment

  
  
  

### **Preferred Qualifications:**

* Experience with large-scale vision-language models, self-supervised learning, or generative image and video modeling
* Demonstrated software engineering experience through internships, open-source contributions, or research engineering roles
* Experience with 3D vision tasks including depth estimation, novel view synthesis, neural radiance fields, or multi-view reconstruction
* Proven track record of publications at leading computer vision or machine learning venues such as CVPR, ICCV, ECCV, NeurIPS, ICML, or SIGGRAPH

Meta builds technologies that help people connect, find communities, and grow businesses. When Facebook launched in 2004, it changed the way people connect. jobs.title: Founding Research Engineer
jobs.description:
**About Raindrop**
==================

Raindrop is the monitoring platform for AI agents. Engineering teams at Fortune 100s and the fastest-growing AI companies (Vercel, Speak, Clay) use it to catch silent failures in production. When an agent misbehaves, Raindrop alerts the team, links to the trace, and surfaces the root cause so they can fix it fast. With Raindrop 2.0 (Self-Healing Agents), the loop closes itself: your coding agent fixes it, and the fix becomes an eval to prevent regressions.

**Why It Matters**
==================

AI agents fail constantly in ways both hilarious and terrifying. Regular software throws exceptions. But AI agents fail silently, leaving engineers with almost no visibility into how their agents are actually performing.

The current status quo is sifting through millions of logs and trying to debug flaky evals that just aren't matching real world results. Evals are like unit tests, they confirm your model got specific test cases right. But in the real world agents call thousands of tools, run for hours, and encounter millions of unpredictable actions.

That’s where Raindrop comes in. It learns the unique shape of each AI agent’s issues. Starting from presets like Laziness, Forgetting, or Task Failure, to automatically tuning itself to each agent and discovering unknown unknowns.

With one click of a button, AI engineers start tracking issues or topics across 100% of their production data. They can see frequency over time, how many users are affected, relevant properties and more.

In order to process hundreds of millions of events, we gradually train small, custom models, private to each company, that learn to uniquely understand how their product is used.

As part of the early team, you’ll play a fundamental role in shaping the company - from making strategy and product decisions, to helping scale the team, to shaping the future of AI agents.

**Our Investors**
=================

We've raised $50M total, led by CRV, with backing from Lightspeed, Figma Ventures, Vercel Ventures, and the founders of Replit (Amjad Masad, Michele Catasta), Cognition (Walden Yan), Framer (Koen Bok, Jorn van Dijk), Speak (Andrew Hsu), and Notion (Akshay Kothari).

**About the role:**

We’re looking for a founding Research Engineer to study how AI agents behave in production. You’ll join an early team, set the research agenda, and publish what we learn.

**Your Focus:**

* **Agent behavior**: Discover how agents fail and respond to different conditions in the real world, and what that means for monitoring and safety.
* **Simulations**: Advance how we simulate agents and the situations they face before they reach users.
* **Detection**: Develop new methods for finding issues no one has defined yet.
* **Open questions**: High-upside bets on questions about agents we haven’t thought to ask yet.

**Your responsibilities:**

* Set Raindrop’s research agenda and run the experiments behind it.
* Design evaluations and metrics for problems where the ground truth is unclear.
* Publish findings as papers, blog posts, and talks.
* Prototype new methods, and bring the ones that work into the product when it makes sense.
* Help define what research looks like at Raindrop as the team and product grows.

**Ideal Candidate:**

* You make complex ideas clear through strong written and communication skills.
* Care about sharing your research through publications, open-source work, or public write-ups.
* Deep expertise in an area such as interpretability, evals, AI safety, anomaly detection, or representation learning.
* Good judgment about which experiments are worth running and when a result is real.
* You ship experiments and build prototypes
* Use and build AI agents and tools

jobs.description:
**Company Description**

**We help the world run better**

At SAP, we keep it simple: you bring your best to us, and we'll bring out the best in you. We're builders touching over 20 industries and 80% of global commerce, and we need your unique talents to help shape what's next. The work is challenging – but it matters. You'll find a place where you can be yourself, prioritize your wellbeing, and truly belong. What's in it for you? Constant learning, skill growth, great benefits, and a team that wants you to grow and succeed.

 **Job Description**

**Teach AI how business actually works**

AI agents are starting to take on real business work: releasing blocked invoices, re-planning supply, preparing the financial close. To do it safely, they need more than access to data. They need to know what an order, a supplier and a cost center are, how they connect, which rules and authorizations apply, and what happened the last time someone made a similar decision. When executing mission-critical business processes, an answer or action that is right 90% of the time is not good enough.

SAP systems hold the context for many of the world's largest companies. SAP's knowledge graph for SAP S/4HANA alone is based on 452,000 tables, 80,000 CDS views (semantic data models) and 7.3 million fields. Yet much of the meaning, especially in each company's own extensions, configuration and decision history, is still implicit. A 'customer' in sales, a 'business partner' in finance and an 'account' in CRM can be the same company described three ways, and an agent deciding whether to raise a credit limit has to know that. This is not a data-cleaning problem, it is a knowledge-representation problem. Today that context, the semantic layer agents rely on, is mostly modeled by hand, one company at a time. We think it can be learned, so AI agents can act on business data, not just read it. SAP's Autonomous Enterprise depends on that, and it is what makes the agents people work with in Joule Work, SAP’s AI workspace, accurate enough to trust.

As a Senior Data Scientist, you'll own a research thread end to end: from an open question, to a method and a benchmark, to a prototype a product team adopts. This is a research and modeling role, not product analytics.

**SAP Research & Innovation North America**

We are a team of scientists and engineers at SAP Labs in Palo Alto, minutes from Stanford. We look a few years ahead and scout emerging technologies, take the early, riskier bets that product teams can’t always take, and prove or drop them fast. SAP’s product teams build and run SAP Knowledge Graph, we look beyond and find and prove methods that demonstrate improvement or paradigm shifts. Our job is to spot the opportunities that will matter most to SAP and our customers, and to get there early. We prototype with dedicated GPU compute on realistic business data and, in co-innovation projects, on real data for training and evaluating models. We publish research, work with startups, universities and institutes including Stanford HAI and UC Irvine, and hand what works to SAP's product teams. We move like a small lab, with the reach of a company whose software runs finance, supply chain and HR for many of the world's largest companies.

**What you will work on**

* **Research you own.** Take an open question from ambiguous framing to a reproducible result, and decide what to do next based on what you find. Closely collaborate with top universities and institutes such as Stanford HAI.
* **What comes next.** Reproduce promising new papers on SAP data within weeks and recommend which deserve a bigger bet.
* **Better ways to build the semantic layer agents need.** New methods to learn and maintain ontologies of business objects, processes, rules and actions, with SAP's semantic models as the backbone and LLMs, schema matching and entity resolution to extend them.
* **Agents grounded in business context.** Graph-augmented retrieval and text-to-query agents (SQL, SPARQL, APIs) over very large schemas, with checks against business rules and access rights, and governed actions.
* **Models that learn from relational data.** Graph neural networks and relational foundation models, such as SAP-RPT-1.6, applied with knowledge-graph context to prediction, anomaly detection and what-if analysis.
* **Honest measurement.** Datasets, benchmarks and evaluation harnesses that show whether an approach works on realistic enterprise data, and why, using synthetic or privacy-preserving data where real data can't be shared.
* **Work others can use.** Clean Python that others build on, prototypes built together with (and adopted by) product and engineering teams, published research papers or open-source releases, and mentoring for interns.

**In your first year, success could look like:**

* Own one research thread end to end, hands on. For example, schema linking for agents over SAP finance data, taken from baseline to benchmark to a prototype a product team adopts.
* A paper submission or open-source release.

This is a senior individual-contributor role, comparable to Senior Research or Data Scientist at other Bay Area technology companies.

 **Qualifications**

**Required**

* Typically 5+ years of hands-on data science, machine learning or applied research, or a PhD plus 2+ years, taking projects from an open question to a measurable result. An MS or PhD in computer science, machine learning, statistics, mathematics or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
* Hands-on depth in at least one of the following, and an appetite to learn the others:
  + Knowledge graphs, ontologies or semantic layers: RDF, OWL, SHACL, SPARQL, or property graphs with Cypher or similar
  + Entity resolution, schema matching or data integration
  + Machine learning on relational, graph or tabular data, including GNNs

jobs.description:
**DESCRIPTION**
---------------

Amazon’s Center for Quantum Computing (CQC) is building the next generation of quantum computing hardware.
  
  
The Center for Quantum Computing (CQC) is our longest-horizon bet and operates at the intersection of hardware and physics. The goal is a quantum computer that could solve in hours what today's most robust machines would take thousands of years to compute, unlocking breakthroughs in myriad of areas ranging from advanced materials for batteries to cryptography and fundamentally-secure data sharing protocols. This program involves R&D in device theory, materials science, nano-scale fabrication, superconducting circuit design, cryogenic refrigeration, and quantum algorithms and applications.
  
  
Currently, the quantum hardware team is focused on improving the underlying chip fabrication of the quantum processor and the scaling of the control system needed to run large-scale quantum circuits. As part of this effort, the team is expanding its chip fabrication capabilities through the construction of a new cleanroom facility dedicated to superconducting quantum chip fabrication, and working with strategic partners to develop scaled versions of the control electronics, I/O wiring, and cryogenic refrigeratation needed for utility-scale quantum computers.
  
  
We operate with a startup-like pace inside one of the world's most capable technology organizations, combining the urgency of a competitive frontier with the resources and infrastructure of pan Amazon.
  
  
We are seeking an Applied Scientist III to join our team and drive the design, construction, and operation of quantum processors. You will work alongside world-class physicists and engineers to push the frontier of quantum computing — from laser system design and atom trapping to high-fidelity gate execution and quantum error correction. This is a rare opportunity to be part of shaping a technology that could define the next era of computing.
  
  
Key job responsibilities  

* Design, build, and operate quantum computing experiments, including optical trapping arrays, laser cooling and state-preparation systems, and high-fidelity gate-driving optics

  

* Develop and optimize two-qubit entangling gates using interactions, targeting fidelities at or beyond the current state of the art (>99.5%)

  

* Implement and characterize erasure-detection protocols leveraging the metastable-state structure of ¹⁷¹Yb to achieve hardware-native erasure conversion rates >90%

  

* Contribute to quantum error correction experiments, including surface codes and quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) codes, and work toward demonstrating error suppression factors (Λ) well beyond current published records

  

* Design and improve atom-array loading, rearrangement, and continuous replenishment techniques to support registers of thousands to tens of thousands of atoms

  

* Develop control software and calibration routines for high-speed experimental sequences, including real-time feedback and adaptive protocols

  

* Analyze experimental data, build physical models to explain observed behavior, and propose and execute improvements to system performance

  

* Collaborate with theory, software, and hardware engineering teams to co-design quantum architectures, error-correcting codes, and decoder systems

  

* Publish results in leading scientific journals and present at top conferences to maintain Amazon's visibility in the quantum research community

**DESCRIPTION**
---------------

Core to Amazon's DNA is its methodology around executing experiments and prototypes to find the quickest way to prove new ideas, technologies, and business models in a real-world environment. Experimentation fuels Amazon's innovation.  
  
Our team does horizon exploration. We take emerging technology, including our own inventions, build working prototypes with customers and partners, and demonstrate what becomes possible before the rest of the market gets there. Prototyping is how we do the work. Pushing the technology horizon is why we do it.  
  
If you are a highly creative problem solver who works to inspire, motivate, and define innovative solutions; are passionate about technology, understand cloud architectures and platforms, and are quick to pick up emerging technologies; are adept at working with customers to experiment with innovative approaches and validate the technical feasibility of solutions, this could be the role for you.  
  
As a Senior Applied Scientist you sit directly with customers and partners. You help them envision complex uses of AWS by building working prototypes of specific use cases, tailored to their data, devices, and systems. Engagements run in short build cycles, typically four to six weeks, and are designed to be innovative and evaluative, demonstrating the art of the possible on AWS while proving a credible path to production.  
  
You will work across the areas where we are placing our biggest bets. These shift as the technology does, but today they include:  

* Physical AI and autonomous robotics. World models, vision-language-action (VLA) models, cloud-based and agentic VLA, real-to-sim and sim-to-real pipelines, and agentic control of physical systems. We challenge the assumption that these models have to live only at the edge.
* Autonomous scientific discovery. Self-driving labs and instrument intelligence, where agents plan, run, and interpret experiments across fleets of scientific instruments.
* Agentic developer intelligence. Multi-agent systems, code agents, and automated research workflows that change how software gets built.

ambiguous_jobs.description:
### **Minimum qualifications:**

* Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Mathematics, Applied Statistics, Machine Learning or equivalent practical experience.
* 5 years of experience with TensorFlow or similar ML frameworks (e.g., JAX or PyTorch).
* 2 years of experience in an applied research setting.

  

### **Preferred qualifications:**

* Experience with training diffusion models.
* Experience working in industry and on projects from proof-of-concept through to implementation.

**About the job**
-----------------

At Google, research-focused Software Engineers are embedded throughout the company, allowing them to setup large-scale tests and deploy promising ideas quickly and broadly. Ideas may come from internal projects as well as from collaborations with research programs at partner universities and technical institutes all over the world.  
  
From creating experiments and prototyping implementations to designing new architectures, engineers work on real-world problems including artificial intelligence, data mining, natural language processing, hardware and software performance analysis, improving compilers for mobile platforms, as well as core search and much more. But you stay connected to your research roots as an active contributor to the wider research community by partnering with universities and publishing papers. Artificial intelligence will be one of humanity’s most transformative inventions. At Google DeepMind, we are a pioneering AI lab with exceptional interdisciplinary teams focused on advancing AI development to solve complex global challenges and accelerate high-quality product innovation for billions of users. We use our technologies for widespread public benefit and scientific discovery, ensuring safety and ethics are always our highest priority.  
  
We are pushing the boundaries across multiple domains. Our global teams offer diverse learning opportunities and varied career pathways for those driven to achieve exceptional results through collective effort.Individual pay is determined by factors including job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training.
  
  
US: $174000 - $252000 (USD) + 15% bonus target + equity + benefits  
  
Learn more about benefits at Google.

**Responsibilities**
--------------------

* Lead ambitious team collaborations, aligning efforts across DeepMind to execute on shared, high-impact research goals.
* Report and present complex research breakthroughs clearly and efficiently.
* Build, lead, and maintain strategic collaborations with key external research labs and leading individuals in the field.
* Act as a principal representative of our work internally and externally at global venues.

Google is proud to be an equal opportunity workplace and is an affirmative action employer. We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status, disability, gender identity or Veteran status. We also consider qualified applicants regardless of criminal histories, consistent with legal requirements. See also Google's EEO Policy and EEO is the Law. If you have a disability or special need that requires accommodation, please let us know by completing our Accommodations for Applicants form.
